vaisakhi.s: Vaisakhi, or Baisakhi, is a spring harvest festival of the Punjab and one of the most important festivals of the Sikh calendar, commemorating the founding of the Khalsa. In 1801, on the day of Vaisakhi, Ranjit Singh was proclaimed Maharaja of the Punjab at Lahore.

vaishali.s: Vaishali was an ancient city in the north of present-day Bihar in eastern India, associated with the early Buddhist and Jain traditions. In the Gupta period it was an important urban centre.

vakil.s: Vakil was a Persian title meaning deputy or regent, used for a high office of state in Safavid Iran. The Zand ruler Karim Khan adopted it rather than the title of Shah, presenting himself as regent rather than king.

vakil-al-ruaya.s: Vakil al-Ruaya, meaning Regent of the People, was the title adopted by Karim Khan, founder of the Zand Empire. The Zand Empire profile explains that he refused to take the title of Shah.

vakil-bath.s: The Vakil Bath is a historic public bathhouse in Shiraz, Iran, built under Karim Khan during the Zand period. It forms part of the architectural ensemble with which he adorned his capital.

vakil-bazaar.s: The Vakil Bazaar is the main covered market of Shiraz, Iran, built under Karim Khan during the Zand period. Its vaulted brick arcades formed the commercial heart of the Zand capital.

vakil-mosque.s: The Vakil Mosque is a mosque in Shiraz, Iran, built under Karim Khan during the Zand period, next to the Vakil Bazaar. It is noted for its prayer hall of carved stone columns and its tile decoration.

valencia.s: Valencia is a city on the Mediterranean coast of eastern Spain, surrounded by a fertile irrigated plain known as the huerta. In the medieval period it was an important city of al-Andalus.

valens.s: Valens was Roman emperor in the east from 364 until his death in 378 CE. He allowed Gothic refugees to cross the Danube into the empire, but their mistreatment led to revolt.

valerian.s: Valerian was a Roman emperor of the mid-third century CE who campaigned against the Sasanian Empire. In 260 CE he was captured by the Sasanian king Shapur I after the Battle of Edessa, becoming the first Roman emperor taken prisoner by a foreign enemy.

valladolid-debate.s: The Valladolid debate was a formal dispute held in Spain in 1550–1551 on the treatment of the indigenous peoples of the Americas. Bartolomé de las Casas defended their rights and humanity, while Juan Ginés de Sepúlveda argued that their conquest and subjugation were justified.

valley-of-mexico.s: The Valley of Mexico is a highland basin in central Mexico that once contained a system of shallow lakes, including Lake Texcoco. It was densely populated and home to many city-states.

vandal-conquest-of-north-africa.s: The Vandal conquest of North Africa was the seizure of Roman Africa by the Vandals and Alans between 429 and 439 CE. Crossing from Spain under King Gaiseric, they captured Carthage in 439 and established a kingdom that controlled much of the western Mediterranean.

vandals.s: The Vandals were a Germanic people who migrated through Gaul and Spain before crossing into North Africa in 429 CE. They established a kingdom centred on Carthage and sacked Rome in 455 CE.

vanuatu.s: Vanuatu is an island nation in the south-western Pacific Ocean, formerly known as the New Hebrides. It was governed as an Anglo-French condominium.

varna.s: Varna is the classical Indian system dividing society into four broad orders: Brahmins (priests), Kshatriyas (warriors and rulers), Vaishyas (merchants and farmers) and Shudras (labourers and servants). It was set out in Sanskrit religious and legal texts.

vasco-da-gama.s: Vasco da Gama was a Portuguese navigator who led the first European voyage to reach India by sea, arriving at Calicut in 1498 after rounding the Cape of Good Hope. His voyage opened a direct maritime route between Europe and Asia.

vassal.s: A vassal is a ruler or lord who holds power or land in subordination to a superior, owing loyalty, tribute or military service in return for protection or recognition. Vassalage was a widespread means of extending imperial authority without direct administration.

vassal-and-tributary-systems.s: Vassal and tributary systems describe the recurring pattern by which empires ruled indirectly through subordinate rulers who kept local authority in exchange for tribute, military service and acknowledgement of overlordship. Such systems allowed rapid expansion at low cost but…

vastryoshan.s: The vastryoshan were the commoners in the social hierarchy of the Sasanian Empire, comprising both peasant cultivators and artisans. The Sasanian Empire profile explains that society was divided into four estates: priests, warriors, scribes and administrators, and commoners.

venetia.s: Venetia is a historical region of north-eastern Italy centred on Venice. After the Napoleonic Wars it was ruled by the Austrian Empire as part of the Kingdom of Lombardy–Venetia.

venice.s: Venice is a city in north-eastern Italy built on islands in a lagoon, which became a major maritime and commercial republic in the medieval period. Venetian merchants gained extensive trading privileges in the Byzantine Empire from 1082, and Venice played a leading role in the…

verden.s: Verden is a town in Lower Saxony, northern Germany, historically the seat of a prince-bishopric. Under the Peace of Westphalia in 1648, Sweden received the bishoprics of Bremen and Verden, together with Wismar and western Pomerania.

versailles.s: Versailles is a town near Paris and the site of the vast palace built by Louis XIV, which became the seat of the French court and a symbol of absolute monarchy. In 1871 the German Empire was proclaimed in its Hall of Mirrors after the defeat of France.

viceroy-of-india.s: A viceroy is an official who governs a country or province in the name of a monarch. The title is best known for the Viceroy of India, the head of British government in India after 1858, who governed the Raj with the Indian Civil Service.

viceroy-of-kush.s: The Viceroy of Kush, also called the King's Son of Kush, was the official who governed Nubia on behalf of the pharaoh during Egypt's New Kingdom. The Egyptian Empire New Kingdom profile describes the office as a semi-autonomous imperial sub-administration.

viceroy-of-portuguese-india.s: The Viceroy of Portuguese India was the governor of the Estado da Índia, the Portuguese colonial administration in Asia, based at Goa from the early sixteenth century. The Portuguese Empire profile notes that his authority nominally extended over all Portuguese possessions…

viceroyalty-of-new-spain.s: The Viceroyalty of New Spain was the administrative unit of the Spanish Empire covering Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean, parts of what is now the United States and later the Philippines. It was established in 1535 with its capital at Mexico City.

viceroyalty-of-peru.s: The Viceroyalty of Peru was the administrative unit of the Spanish Empire created in 1542 to govern most of Spanish South America, with its capital at Lima. Its silver mines, especially Potosí, made it a principal source of imperial revenue.

victory-stele-of-naram-sin.s: The Victory Stele of Naram-Sin is a carved stone monument celebrating the Akkadian king Naram-Sin's victory over the Lullubi mountain people, showing the king ascending a mountain above his defeated enemies. It is a masterpiece of Akkadian art.

vienna.s: Vienna is the capital of Austria, on the Danube, and was for centuries the seat of the Habsburg monarchy. It withstood Ottoman sieges in 1529 and 1683, the second of which was broken with the help of a Polish-Lithuanian relief army under Jan III Sobieski.

vienna-secession.s: The Vienna Secession was an art movement founded in 1897 by Gustav Klimt and other artists who broke away from Vienna's established academic art association. It promoted modern styles in painting, architecture and design.

viet-minh.s: The Viet Minh was a Vietnamese independence movement founded in 1941 under the leadership of Ho Chi Minh. It fought against Japanese occupation and then against the restoration of French colonial rule in the First Indochina War.

vietnam.s: Vietnam is a country in mainland Southeast Asia along the eastern coast of the Indochinese peninsula. Its northern part was long under Chinese rule, including periods of Han and Tang administration, and it absorbed Confucian governance traditions.

vijayanagara-empire.s: The Vijayanagara Empire was a powerful Hindu state in southern India founded around 1336, with its capital at Vijayanagara on the Tungabhadra River. It arose as Delhi Sultanate control over the Deccan and the south weakened.

vikings.s: The Vikings were seafaring Scandinavians who raided, traded and settled across Europe from the late eighth to the eleventh centuries. Their raids devastated the coasts and river valleys of the divided Carolingian kingdoms, and the Carolingian Empire profile notes Charles the…

villa-estate.s: A villa, in the Carolingian context, was a great landed estate belonging to the church, the crown or the aristocracy. The Carolingian Empire profile describes these villae as the primary units of agricultural production and local governance.

virginia.s: Virginia is a region on the Atlantic coast of North America, named in honour of Queen Elizabeth I. The colony founded at Jamestown in 1607 was the first permanent English settlement in America.

vishaya.s: A vishaya was an administrative district in the Gupta Empire and other early Indian states. The Gupta Empire profile explains that the provinces, or bhuktis, governed by uparikas were subdivided into vishayas.

vishayapati.s: A vishayapati was the official in charge of a vishaya, or district, in the Gupta Empire. The Gupta Empire profile notes that vishayapatis were often drawn from local merchant guilds, working beneath the provincial governors known as uparikas.

vishnugupta.s: Vishnugupta was the last recognised emperor of the Gupta dynasty, ruling around 540–550 CE. By his time the empire had been reduced to a remnant kingdom by Huna invasions, succession disputes and the rise of regional powers.

visigoths.s: The Visigoths were a Gothic Germanic people who entered the Roman Empire in the late fourth century. They destroyed a Roman army and killed Emperor Valens at Adrianople in 378 CE, and under Alaric they sacked Rome in 410 CE.

vizier.s: A vizier is a high minister or chief administrator serving a ruler, a title used in many Islamic states and applied by historians to the chief officials of ancient Egypt. In the Abbasid Caliphate the vizier headed the bureaucracy, and the Seljuk vizier Nizam al-Mulk became the…

vo-nguyen-giap.s: Vo Nguyen Giap was a Vietnamese military commander, the principal general of the Viet Minh and later of North Vietnam. He led the Viet Minh forces in the First Indochina War against France.

volga.s: The Volga is the longest river in Europe, flowing through central Russia to the Caspian Sea. It was a major artery of trade linking the Baltic and northern forests with the Caspian, Central Asia and the Islamic world.

volga-trade-route.s: The Volga trade route was a network of river and portage routes linking Scandinavia and the Baltic with the Caspian Sea and the Islamic world via the Volga River in the early medieval period. Furs, slaves and other goods moved south, while silver dirhams flowed north.

volhynia.s: Volhynia is a historical region in north-western Ukraine. It formed part of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania until 1569.

volta-river.s: The Volta is a river system of West Africa that flows south through present-day Ghana to the Gulf of Guinea. The Oyo Empire profile notes that around 1748, at the height of Oyo power, its tributary network stretched from the Niger River in the east to the Volta corridor in the…

voorcompagnieen.s: The voorcompagnieën, or pre-companies, were the Dutch trading companies formed in the 1590s to send ships to Asia before the creation of the Dutch East India Company. Their competition drove up prices in Asia and lowered profits in Europe.
